questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I had read on internet that KU Leuven that is a really old university, from 1425 is considered a really good university and that Leuven is a great place for students because there are students from all over the world. 
I also found it important for career purposes to study somewhere else and get acquainted with other universities and cultures. 
It was also nice to visit some of the cultural places of the Low Countries as well as be able to visit the European Parliament and see how things work.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: KU Leuven is world known university and therefor I immediately found out that it would be a nice place to study. But it also always good idea to search on facebook or instagram to find out more about the different universities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We started by having Orientation days where were received some practical information, and we had also the possibility of writing to a Buddy who was a student from the city to meet and ask questions if we wanted to.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university had given us possibilities to contact different landlords with whom they were cooperating.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I have never lived on campus so I do not know what the differences are, but before going they should make a plan about the most important things that they need for a few months, and they should not take too much of unnecessary things.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
There was always a possibility for meeting and talking to the person who helps the international students. 
They will during the first week inform about the necessary steps to be taken. 
It was possible to attend classes during the first week, where we were encouraged to attend as many as possible, ask the teachers about different things and decide what we wanted to study.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I was possible to contact the person who was organizing things for exchange students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I chose very interesting classes and almost completely changed my mind about what I beforehand had decided to study and the first week where I attended many classes was very helpful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advice to attend many classes and ask about possibilities, because I took a few classes that were master classes, as I had been informed that I could do that because I am a 3rd year student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In the beginning it was hard to find out how it was compared to the University of Copenhagen, because it seemed to be easier, but we were from the beginning informed not to expect too high grades. Out written exams were written in hand which was very different from what I am used to and it turned out after all that it was not as difficult as we were being told. Nevertheless, it is important to study a few hours a day to keep up.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style was different I personally prefer our own university (of Copenhagen). There was less of group work and discussion during the classes, and the classrooms were also different and that also made class discussions a bit more difficult as we sat differently.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Highlights in European Literature 
Political Philosophy 
International relations after WWII 
Flemish Art 
Culture and Emotions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all of them. There teachers were very nice and helpful and it was always possible to ask them questions. 
Flemish art was very important in understanding the culture of the Low Countries, and International relations was mainly about the establishment of the institutions of the EU which was very interesting especially because a lot of them are in Brussels.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were a few things that I had not planned to buy like a blanket for example, but I would also recommend using money on buying tickets to visit other cities (and even maybe countries around Belgium).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was more expensive than I had expected but I had also rented a room with personal bathroom.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there were not many activities other than bars for students and cultural activities, but it did not seem like many were participating. There were also sometimes trips organized by the teachers to museums or other places.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bars were available, there are in Leuven a lot of nice places to eat and a lot of nice chocolate shops, especially in Bruges.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend to use some time on studying and visiting other cities such as bruges, Antwerp, Brussels, Paris etc. There are lots of nice shops for chocolate, sweets, arts things like tapestries, cards, local cultural things to buy as souvenirs.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit unusual because they behaved differently from the Danes, but were nevertheless nice to be around.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Arrange trips or thing to do in the weekend 
Go to bars and cafes

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It is easier to communicate with the Danes but in general they too are very nice.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I liked the way the shops and architecture was arranged, because it meant something for hoe it felt to spend time when alone without people with whom one is used to spend time, especially during the weekends

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
I would tell them to attend as many classes as possible before choosing what they want to study 
I would tell them to ask the teachers about the exams and their expectations at the beginning 
I would tell them that the exams are written in hand and that they should be prepared for that

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: To know that some of the things that they need to buy they might find cheaper from other students selling their stuff.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It allows one to think that he or she has much more experience of studying elsewhere and having learnt to do it their way and it gives courage to braver in the future. It may also be important for future career.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be far away from home and have no one to talk to if the exams seems difficult for example, but it is always a good idea to contact the teachers or the person who helps the exchange students.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
